s1.syndrome_frame: Abdominal pain and mass with submucosal bulging and ulcerated areas
salient_findings: Palpable, movable mass in the upper abdomen
Large echogenic mass in the gastric antrum on abdominal ultrasound
Large submucosal bulging mass in the posterior gastric wall with ulcerated areas on endoscopy
key_facts: 63-year-old woman with insidious upper abdominal pain
Pain unrelated to food ingestion
Nausea
Episode of intense acute abdominal pain
No hematemesis or melena
Untreated dyslipidemia
Well-controlled hypertension on methyldopa
Smoker of ten cigarettes per day
No family history of cancer
Normal physical examination except for palpable mass
Normal laboratory tests, including complete blood count
No anemia
Abdominal ultrasound showed large echogenic mass in gastric antrum
Endoscopy revealed large submucosal bulging mass with ulcerated areas
Biopsy attempts failed to sample submucosal mass
Ulcer biopsies showed only necrotic mucosa
Contrast-enhanced CT showed well-defined, homogeneous, oval mass arising from posterior gastric wall

shortlist.label: Gastric lipoma
shortlist.why_kept: Large echogenic mass in gastric antrum with fat-tissue attenuation on CT

shortlist.label: Gastrointestinal stromal tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Submucosal bulging mass with ulcerated areas and large size

shortlist.label: Leiomyoma
shortlist.why_kept: Submucosal mass with well-defined borders and homogeneous appearance on CT

shortlist.label: Liposarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Large size and central contrast enhancement of the mass

shortlist.label: Gastric schwannoma
shortlist.why_kept: Submucosal mass with well-defined borders and potential for ulceration

raw.rationale: The abdominal ultrasound and contrast-enhanced CT showing a large echogenic mass with fat-tissue attenuation and the absence of invasion into peripheral layers support this diagnosis

rejected.label: Gastrointestinal stromal tumor
rejected.why: Typically has a more aggressive appearance on imaging and may have different attenuation characteristics

rejected.label: Leiomyoma
rejected.why: Usually appears as a well-defined, solid mass without fat attenuation on CT

rejected.label: Liposarcoma
rejected.why: Although considered due to large size and central contrast enhancement, the lack of invasion and homogeneous fat attenuation on CT makes this less likely

rejected.label: Gastric schwannoma
rejected.why: Not directly supported by the imaging findings described, which emphasize fat-tissue attenuation
